# Offline screening reference fixtures

The `references/` FASTA and reduced NCBI taxonomy files and `sim_1.fq` / `sim_2.fq` are unmodified files from the MIT-licensed [official Kraken2 test corpus](https://github.com/DerrickWood/kraken2/tree/e1a819d985d1a257e20a8fc57eb27a5d51f4c39e), pinned at that commit. Upstream describes 38 viral sequences and 40 taxa, with NCBI-derived content modified by upstream for minimal fixture size/Kraken identifiers. Simulation files contain 400 simulated pairs, 20 chimeric tie pairs and 20 random pairs. They are **simulated**, not experimental specimens.

`genuine-kraken2-2.17.1.tsv` is actual output of the source-pinned serial build (reported version 2.17.1), run on `sim_1.fq` with the reduced database. It reports 440 processed single reads, 419 classified and 21 unclassified. This is a parser regression fixture, not invented production metrics or an accuracy claim for real assays. `source-provenance.json` records original file hashes, source paths, actual capture parameters and database hashes. The captured database used upstream default masking; the portable explicit test-builder variant uses no masking and records its own hashes. Real adapter tests compare against an independent command using the exact same current database rather than assuming the two variants are identical.

The paired `SRR6357070_first100_R*.fastq.gz` files contain the first 100 original records from each public nf-core GSE110004/SRR6357070 test file at commit `cad884e7fbe5617dcd55bdd07d9ddf65b54febe4`. Upstream already filtered/subsampled the experimental yeast RNA-seq data to chrI. No read identifiers, bases or qualities were changed; output gzip mtime is zero. `experimental-provenance.json` records original/subset checksums and exact derivation. The nf-core license is retained in `YEAST-LICENSE`.

These small subsets and the viral-only database are for software fidelity/coverage tests, **not production contamination assessment**, full-run inference, or a reference covering yeast/human/all microbes. No tool binaries or generated database binaries are checked in. Build the offline fixture with an explicitly supplied tool using `scripts/prepare-screening-test-db.py`; production startup does not install/build/download anything.
